name: הפרדת משתנים – פתרון כללי עם tanh (ב) (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Solve the following differential equation:

\[ \frac{dy}{dx} - {{CT:0}} -{{CT:1}}x^2+{{CT:2}}y^2+y^2x^2 = 0. \]

Use the letter \(c\) to denote the arbitrary constant occuring in the general solution.

\( y(x) = \) [[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]

How to enter: a square root as sqrt(...), e.g. sqrt(5*x). Other roots as a power, with brackets around the exponent: \(\sqrt[3]{x+1}\) is entered as (x+1)^(1/3).
generalfeedback:
Outline: factorise the right-hand side as \(g(y)h(x)\), separate the variables, integrate the left-hand side with a \(\tanh\) substitution and solve for \(y\).
Step 1 — Factorising and separating
Rearranging the differential equation gives

\[ \frac{dy}{dx}-{{CT:1}}({{CT:2}}+x^2)+y^2({{CT:2}}+x^2)=0 \]

and therefore

\[ \frac{dy}{dx}=({{CT:1}}-y^2)({{CT:2}}+x^2), \]

so that

\[ \frac{dy}{{{CT:1}}-y^2}=({{CT:2}}+x^2)dx. \]

Integrating both sides yields:

\[ \int\frac{dy}{{{CT:1}}-y^2}=\int({{CT:2}}+x^2)dx \]

Step 2 — The left-hand side: a tanh substitution
To integrate the left hand side, rearrange

\[ \frac{dy}{{{CT:1}}-y^2}=\frac{dy}{{{CT:1}}(1-\frac{y^2}{{CT:1}})} \]

Let \(\frac{y}{{CT:3}} = \tanh(u)\)

\[ \frac{dy}{{CT:3}}=(1-\tanh^2(u))du = (1-\frac{y^2}{{CT:1}})du \]

\[ \frac{dy}{(1-\frac{y^2}{{CT:1}})}={{CT:3}}du. \]

Therefore

\[ \int\frac{dy}{{{CT:1}}-y^2}=\frac{1}{{CT:1}}\int\frac{dy}{{CT:4}}=\frac{1}{{CT:1}}\int{{CT:3}}du=\frac{u}{{CT:3}}. \]

Step 3 — The right-hand side
Integrating the right hand side gives

\[ \int({{CT:2}}+x^2)dx={{CT:2}}x+\frac{x^3}{3}+c. \]

Therefore

\[ \frac{u}{{CT:3}}={{CT:2}}x+\frac{x^3}{3}+c, \]

so that

\[ u={{CT:3}}\left({{CT:2}}x+\frac{x^3}{3}+c\right) \]

and hence

\[ \tanh(u)=\tanh\left({{CT:3}}\left({{CT:2}}x+\frac{x^3}{3}+c\right)\right) \]

Step 4 — The general solution
Therefore

\[ \frac{y}{{CT:3}}=\tanh\left({{CT:3}}\left({{CT:2}}x+\frac{x^3}{3}+c\right)\right) \]

and

\[ y={{CT:5}} \]
